digest.headline: Ten-year US Treasury yields topped 5 percent as the Federal Reserve held interest rates.

lede.b: The 10-year Treasury yield, which is the interest paid by the US government on 10-year loans, climbed above 5.0%. This happened because the Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States that sets official borrowing costs, kept its benchmark interest rate the same. At the same time, the S&P 500 stock index broke through a key support level, which is a price point where a stock or index usually stops falling because buyers step in. Anthropic listed on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker ANT, and US equities rose even as inflation, which measures how fast prices go up, showed the economy growing faster than expected. The 10-year Treasury yield finished the session above 5%.
lede.i: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5.0% after the inflation readings showed faster economic growth and the Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate. S&P 500 equities broke through technical support levels as portfolio managers adjusted allocations following Anthropic's public debut on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker ANT. Technology valuations faced renewed scrutiny amid shifting investment strategies. The 10-year Treasury yield remained above 5.0%.
lede.a: Ten-year Treasury yields breached 5.0% following a Federal Reserve hold and incoming data pointing to robust economic growth. The S&P 500 broke through key support as Anthropic's Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT precipitated portfolio rebalancing and acute scrutiny of technology sector valuations. Fixed-income reallocations by income-seeking capital drove 10-year yields above 5.0% across mixed maturities.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Stocks wobble, Treasury yields hit 5%, and Fed holds

stories.t: S&P 500 Breaks Support as AI Trade Wobbles
stories.b: The S&P 500 index, which groups five hundred large companies, fell below its support level. Support is a price floor where buyers usually step in to stop a drop. A wobbling artificial intelligence trade weighed down these stocks. Anthropic also announced its debut on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker ANT.
stories.i: The S&P 500 broke through key support as a wobbling artificial intelligence trade weighed on equities. Market participants adjusted portfolios following Anthropic's debut on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker ANT. Technology sector valuations faced renewed scrutiny amid shifting investment strategies.
stories.a: The S&P 500 breached technical support as concentration risk in artificial intelligence exposures triggered broader equity liquidations. Anthropic's public listing on the Nasdaq under ticker ANT catalysed a reallocation across tech-heavy indices. Margin pressures intensified as momentum strategies unwound.

stories.t: Ten-Year Treasury Yields Top 5% After Federal Reserve Hold
stories.b: The yield on the 10-year Treasury bond topped 5%. A bond is a loan made by an investor to a government or company, and the yield is the annual return on that loan. Savers hunted for income as yields rose. United States stocks moved up while Treasury yields turned mixed after the Federal Reserve decided to hold interest rates steady.
stories.i: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5% as income-seeking savers reallocated capital. United States equities rose while inflation readings showed the economy growing faster than expected. The Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate, leaving Treasury yields mixed across maturities.
stories.a: The 10-year Treasury yield surpassed 5% driven by robust economic growth prints and sticky price pressures. Duration risk repriced as incoming data showed economic output expanding faster than consensus expectations alongside rising inflation. The Federal Reserve held its policy rate steady, prompting divergent reactions across the sovereign curve.

politics.b: Indiaspora warned that proposed H-1B visa curbs could hurt the United States economy. The group shared concerns about restrictions on skilled foreign workers. Lawmakers and officials weighed the impact of these immigration changes on domestic industries.
politics.i: Indiaspora warned that proposed H-1B visa curbs threaten economic growth. Industry groups highlighted potential disruptions to labour supply chains across technology sectors. Policymakers evaluated the broader implications of tightening skilled migration channels.
politics.a: Indiaspora issued warnings regarding proposed H-1B visa restrictions, citing structural risks to domestic human capital pipelines. Sectoral productivity models indicate potential headwinds if skilled migration inflows face legislative contraction. Labour market tightness concerns compounded lobbying efforts against the proposed regulatory adjustments.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Record bond offerings and currency depreciation

stories.t: Yen Bond Issuance Reaches Record High Amid AI Funding
stories.b: Companies in Japan sold a record $16bn in bonds paid back in yen. A bond is a certificate where an organization borrows money from investors and pays them regular interest. This money helps fund the artificial intelligence race reaching the country. Artificial intelligence refers to computer systems designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence.
stories.i: Corporations issued a record $16bn in yen-denominated debt instruments. This surge aligns with the artificial intelligence funding race expanding into Japan. Borrowers utilize these fixed-income securities to raise capital for technological expansion.
stories.a: Yen-denominated debt issuance hit a record $16bn as artificial intelligence capital expenditure expands domestically. This volume reflects corporate attempts to lock in funding amid shifting liquidity conditions. Credit spreads on these issuances will dictate secondary market demand for tech-sector debt.

politics.b: Japan maintains a high economic standing globally. The country suffers from currency depreciation, meaning its money buys less than before. Officials monitor these financial pressures closely.
politics.i: Japan experiences ongoing currency depreciation despite its high economic standing. Macroeconomic conditions place persistent downward pressure on the valuation of the yen. Policymakers observe these valuation dynamics closely.
politics.a: Persistent currency depreciation undermines domestic purchasing power despite robust economic fundamentals. Structural imbalances continue to pressure the external value of the currency. Foreign exchange valuations remain sensitive to global yield differentials.

China.label: China
China.sub: Corporate earnings and gold prices in China

stories.t: Shenzhen Stock Exchange Reports Third-Quarter Results
stories.b: Shares are units of ownership in a company that people buy and sell. Companies list on a stock exchange to raise money from the public. Exactly 2,904 firms on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange published their financial statements for the third quarter. These businesses generated a combined net profit of 1.08 trillion yuan. Out of those companies, 433 reported double profits.
stories.i: Listed firms on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange finished releasing their periodic financial disclosures. A total of 2,904 companies recorded a combined net profit of 1.08 trillion yuan for the third quarter. Furthermore, 433 of these corporations achieved double profits during the period. This aggregate filing wraps up the reporting cycle for the exchange.
stories.a: The Shenzhen Stock Exchange aggregate third-quarter disclosures cover 2,904 reporting constituents. Aggregate net profits across the cohort reached 1.08 trillion yuan. A subset of 433 enterprises managed double profits during the observation window. These filings conclude the current reporting sequence for the bourse.

stories.t: Kweichow Moutai and GAC Group Announce Financial Updates
stories.b: Liquor maker Kweichow Moutai saw its revenue grow by 3.08% in the third quarter. This return to quarterly growth follows earlier declines. Meanwhile, GAC Group brought in 75.156 billion yuan in revenue over the first three quarters. That figure represents a 12.29% increase driven by domestic brands and overseas shipments.
stories.i: Beverage producer Kweichow Moutai returned to quarterly expansion with third-quarter revenue rising 3.08%. Concurrently, GAC Group posted 75.156 billion yuan in revenue across the first three quarters. This 12.29% top-line increase stemmed from the performance of its proprietary brands and export volumes. Both firms released these figures in their latest operational updates.
stories.a: Kweichow Moutai broke its prior lull with third-order revenue expanding 3.08%. GAC Group reported 75.156 billion yuan in revenue for the first three quarters, marking a 12.29% year-on-year advance. Proprietary marques and export channels served as the primary drivers for the automaker's expansion. These metrics underscore the bifurcation in domestic industrial performance.

stories.t: Gold Prices Drop Below Key Thresholds Globally and Locally
stories.b: International gold prices fell below the $3,900 mark. In domestic markets, Chinese jewelry prices retreated by nearly 550 yuan per gram over the year. Jewelry stores sell gold items directly to consumers based on these per-gram rates. The drop reflects lower global metal valuations.
stories.i: International gold quotes slipped below the $3,900 threshold. Domestic Chinese jewelry retail prices pulled back by nearly 550 yuan per gram across the year. This local retreat mirrors the broader downward movement in international bullion benchmarks. Retail buyers faced significantly lower costs for physical ornaments.
stories.a: Spot gold prices breached the $3,900 per ounce level on international exchanges. Chinese retail jewelry quotes contracted by nearly 550 yuan per gram year-to-date. This adjustment transmits global commodity repricing directly into consumer goods markets. Bullion valuations continue to dictate retail pricing adjustments across local distribution networks.

India.label: India
India.sub: Stock indexes rise as foreign funds buy and bond yields drop

stories.t: Stock indexes climb on foreign buying and lower bond yields
stories.b: Big Indian stock market indexes called the Nifty and Sensex went up by almost 2% recently. This happened because foreign institutional investors, which are large overseas investment funds, started buying more shares. At the same time, bond yields, which are the returns paid on government debt like loans to the state, went down. Lower bond yields often make the stock market look more attractive to investors.
stories.i: The Nifty and Sensex gained nearly 2% driven by foreign institutional investor inflows and falling bond yields. Lower yields reduce the opportunity cost of holding equities, prompting institutional reallocation toward domestic shares. Market participants continue to monitor whether corporate earnings momentum can absorb external cost pressures.
stories.a: Equities rallied close to 2% on the back of foreign institutional investor accumulation and a compression in sovereign bond yields. This compression lowers the discount rate applied to future cash flows, supporting multiple expansion across major indices. Sustainability of the move hinges on whether earnings delivery can offset persistent headwinds from crude prices.

stories.t: Oil prices and import growth shape the path for the rupee
stories.b: The value of the Indian rupee against other currencies depends a lot on international oil prices and how much the country imports from abroad. When oil costs more, the country has to spend more money to buy it. This extra spending affects the currency's overall outlook.
stories.i: The trajectory of the rupee remains tied to global crude oil prices and domestic import growth dynamics. Higher import bills widen the trade deficit, exerting depreciation pressure on the local currency. Analysts continue to assess these macroeconomic factors alongside capital inflows.
stories.a: Rupee valuation hinges on the net current account impact driven by crude price volatility and import expansion. Expansionary import trends combined with elevated energy import bills structurally challenge the domestic currency. Market participants price these external balances against ongoing foreign capital allocations.

politics.b: Market participants and analysts watched company earnings reports and foreign investment flows closely this week.
politics.i: Analysts tracked corporate earnings growth alongside foreign institutional participation to gauge market durability.
politics.a: Market commentary focused on the durability of the earnings-led recovery against the backdrop of global energy costs and cross-border capital flows.
